newsitem.title: UK: Wembley steps up national stadium campaign.
newsitem.headline: Wembley steps up national stadium campaign.

text.p: Wembley Plc, the home of English soccer, pressed its case on Friday to win the battle for selection as the site of Britain's new national stadium.
"Our capital city location is very important. If we are going for the World Cup then playing in the capital is a major advantage," said Wembley chief executive Alan Coppin.
"We are already the de facto national stadium," he added.
Britain's Sports Council is expected to decide on the location for a new national stadium by the end of the year. Wembley, in north London, faces competition from the northern city of Manchester.

The 1920s stadium will be redeveloped at a cost of around 150 million stg if Wembley is chosen. Some 65 percent of that money will come from lottery funding with the rest raised through initiatives such as the sale of debenture seats.
"The atmosphere at Wembley is second to none in the world," said Coppin, adding that he had found the new Amsterdam Arena stadium sterile by comparison on a recent visit.
He defended the stadium against criticisms that it had been allowed to run down, saying that Wembley Plc had invested heavily on facilities such as toilets, bars and shops in recent years.
